references.text: The prohibition against making carved images or representations of anything in heaven, on earth, or in the water – the fundamental commandment against idolatry that Deuteronomy 4:16 expands upon.
Prohibition against making idols, carved images, or cast images – a parallel ban on image worship.
The continuation of the warning in the same chapter against forgetting the covenant and making carved images of any form.
A curse upon anyone who makes a carved or cast image, an abomination to the Lord – the work of a craftsman.
Isaiah's condemnation of those who make god-images and cast idols, which are unable to do anything useful.
The prophet's question about whom one can compare God with, and criticism of those who make god-images.
Paul's speech at the Areopagus that we should not think the divine nature is like gold, silver, or stone, shaped by human art and imagination.
